claim_id: ID of the claim; reused if the same claim has several sources
article_title: Title of the Wikipedia article containing the claim (not the cited source)
claim_text: Exact claim being checked; split compound sentences into separate claims
origin: AI-flagged / Organic sample (how the item was selected, not proof of authorship)
origin_basis: What the label rests on (tool flag, edit summary, reviewer)

annotations.annotation_id: Unique ID for this claim–source evaluation
annotations.source_title: Title as shown by the source
annotations.source_type: Journal article / Thesis / News article / Book / Government report / Fact sheet / Database / Other
annotations.source_access: Full text / Partial / Paywalled / Not found / Other (what you actually inspected)

evidence.excerpt: Short exact quote(s), or NO SUPPORTING PASSAGE FOUND
evidence.location: Page, section or paragraph of the excerpt

annotations.verdict: supported / Partially supported / Not supported / Unable to evaluate
failure_type: One or more of: Missing evidence; Unsupported number/statistic; Unsupported causal link; Overstatement; Unsupported scope or population; Unsupported chronology; Contradiction. Empty if Supported or Unable to evaluate
annotations.rationale: 2–3 sentences naming what the source establishes and what it doesn’t
